events.title: Austronesian Homeland
events.description: Archaeological and linguistic research shows Taiwan as the homeland of Austronesian peoples. Austronesian peoples migrated from Taiwan to the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, and as far as Pacific islands and Madagascar.

events.title: Paleolithic Sites
events.description: Archaeological discoveries show human activity in Taiwan during the Paleolithic period. The Changbin culture sites represent Taiwan's earliest human traces.

events.title: Portuguese Ships Pass Taiwan
events.description: Portuguese sailors passed Taiwan, marveling at the island's beauty and calling it 'Ilha Formosa' (Beautiful Island), from which the name Formosa derived.

events.title: Dutch Occupation of Taiwan
events.description: The Dutch East India Company occupied southern Taiwan, establishing Fort Zeelandia (Anping Fort) and Fort Provintia (Chihkan Tower) in present-day Tainan. The Dutch ruled Taiwan for 38 years, developing agriculture and trade.

events.title: Spanish Occupation of Northern Taiwan
events.description: Spanish occupied northern Taiwan, establishing bases in Keelung and Tamsui. But they were expelled by the Dutch in 1642.

events.title: Koxinga's Campaign
events.description: Ming Dynasty General Koxinga attacked Dutch-occupied Taiwan to resist the Qing and restore the Ming. After a nine-month siege, the Dutch surrendered, and Koxinga established the Kingdom of Tungning, using Taiwan as a base against the Qing.

events.title: Death of Koxinga
events.description: Koxinga died of illness shortly after recovering Taiwan, at only 39 years old. His son Zheng Jing inherited the regime, and the Kingdom of Tungning continued in Taiwan.

events.title: Qing Campaign Against Taiwan
events.description: Qing Dynasty's Shi Lang led naval forces to attack Taiwan, defeating the Tungning navy at the Battle of Penghu. Zheng Keshuang surrendered, the Kingdom of Tungning fell, and Taiwan was incorporated into Qing territory.

events.title: Taiwan Prefecture Established
events.description: The Qing government established Taiwan Prefecture under Fujian Province. This was the first time the Qing formally governed Taiwan, though the government practiced a restrictive immigration policy.

events.title: Zhu Yigui Uprising
events.description: Fujian immigrant Zhu Yigui led a large uprising against Qing rule, briefly occupying Taiwan Prefecture. The rebellion was soon suppressed, but it demonstrated tensions in Taiwan's governance.

events.title: Lin Shuangwen Uprising
events.description: Heaven and Earth Society member Lin Shuangwen led the largest rebellion during Qing rule of Taiwan. The uprising lasted over a year before being suppressed, exposing Taiwan's severe governance problems.

events.title: Treaties of Tianjin Open Taiwan
events.description: After the Second Opium War, the Qing was forced to sign the Treaties of Tianjin, opening Taiwan's ports including Tamsui, Keelung, Anping, and Kaohsiung. Taiwan was drawn into international trade.

events.title: Mudan Incident and Japanese Invasion
events.description: Ryukyuan shipwreck survivors were killed by indigenous people in southern Taiwan. Japan used this as pretext to invade, landing troops in southern Taiwan. Qing paid compensation to resolve the crisis.

events.title: Shen Baozhen Arrives in Taiwan
events.description: Qing court appointed Shen Baozhen as Imperial Commissioner, responsible for Taiwan defense. He promoted modern defense construction and lifted restrictions on mountain area entry.

events.title: Taiwan Becomes a Province
events.description: The Qing government elevated Taiwan from a prefecture to a province, demonstrating increased importance of Taiwan. Liu Mingchuan became Taiwan's first governor, implementing modernization.

events.title: Taiwan Railway Construction Begins
events.description: Governor Liu Mingchuan began Taiwan Railway construction, the first railway in China. Completed in 1893, connecting Keelung to Hsinchu.

events.title: Telegraph System Established
events.description: Taiwan established telegraph system connecting Taiwan with mainland China, and built intra-island networks. This modernized Taiwan's communications significantly.

events.title: Treaty of Shimonoseki Cedes Taiwan
events.description: After Qing defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War, it was forced to sign the Treaty of Shimonoseki, ceding Taiwan and Penghu to Japan. Taiwanese people strongly opposed, triggering anti-Japanese movements.

events.title: Japanese Colonial Period
events.description: Taiwan became Japanese colony, ruled for 50 years. Japan implemented comprehensive modernization of infrastructure, education, medical care, and agriculture, but also exploited resources and suppressed Taiwan's identity.

events.title: Taiwan Democratic Republic Proclaimed
events.description: Taiwanese gentry opposed Japanese occupation, proclaiming the 'Taiwan Democratic Republic' with Tang Jingsong as president. But resistance soon collapsed, and Japanese forces occupied Taiwan.

events.title: Taiwan Bank Established
events.description: The Japanese government established Taiwan Bank as Taiwan's central bank, issuing currency and supporting economic development. The bank played a key role in Taiwan's modernization.

events.title: North-South Railway Completed
events.description: The Taiwan Railway's north-south line was completed, connecting Keelung to Kaohsiung. This greatly promoted Taiwan's economic development and population mobility.

events.title: Taiwan Cultural Association Founded
events.description: Taiwanese intellectuals led by Lin Xiantang founded the Taiwan Cultural Association, promoting cultural enlightenment and Taiwanese self-awareness. This was the beginning of Taiwan's democratic movement.

events.title: Taiwan Parliament Movement
events.description: Taiwanese gentry petitioned the Japanese government to establish a Taiwan parliament, demanding political autonomy. Though never successful, the movement promoted Taiwanese political consciousness.

events.title: Musha Incident
events.description: Seediq people led by Mona Rudao revolted against Japanese rule, attacking the Musha public school sports meet and killing 134 Japanese. Japan violently suppressed the uprising, with hundreds of indigenous people killed.

events.title: Kominka Movement
events.description: After the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese War, Japan implemented the Kominka ('Imperialization') movement in Taiwan, forcing Taiwanese to use Japanese, adopt Japanese names, and worship at shrines, suppressing Taiwanese culture.

events.title: Cairo Declaration
events.description: US President Roosevelt, UK Prime Minister Churchill, and ROC leader Chiang Kai-shek issued the Cairo Declaration, stating that Taiwan and Penghu should be returned to the Republic of China.

events.title: Japanese Surrender and Taiwan's Retrocession
events.description: Japan announced unconditional surrender; Taiwan was liberated from Japanese rule and returned to the Republic of China. The surrender ceremony on October 25 later became 'Taiwan Retrocession Day.'

events.title: Taiwan Retrocession Ceremony
events.description: Japanese Taiwan Governor-General Rikichi Ando signed surrender documents in Taipei, Taiwan officially returned to Republic of China. This day later became 'Taiwan Retrocession Day.'

events.title: 228 Incident
events.description: A tobacco enforcement incident triggered public protests, and government forces opened fire, escalating into island-wide conflict. The incident resulted in thousands to tens of thousands of deaths, devastating Taiwan's social elite. This was postwar Taiwan's most serious political event.

events.title: ROC Government Relocates to Taiwan
events.description: Defeated in the Chinese Civil War, the ROC government relocated to Taiwan. About 2 million soldiers and civilians followed the government to Taiwan, changing Taiwan's demographics and political landscape.

events.title: Martial Law Declared
events.description: Taiwan provincial government declared martial law across Taiwan and Penghu. This was the beginning of the '38-year martial law period,' the longest in world history.

events.title: Korean War Breaks Out, US Protects Taiwan
events.description: The Korean War broke out, US 7th Fleet entered Taiwan Strait to prevent PRC attack on Taiwan. US aid helped Taiwan stabilize and develop economically.

events.title: Land Reform
events.description: The ROC government implemented comprehensive land reform including 'rent reduction to 37.5%,' 'public land sale,' and 'land-to-the-tiller.' This transformed Taiwan's agricultural society and laid foundation for industrialization.

events.title: US-Taiwan Mutual Defense Treaty Signed
events.description: The ROC and US signed the Sino-American Mutual Defense Treaty, with US committed to defending Taiwan and Penghu. This treaty ensured Taiwan's security for decades.

events.title: Second Taiwan Strait Crisis (August 23 Artillery Bombardment)
events.description: The PLA suddenly shelled Kinmen on August 23, beginning 44 days of intense bombardment. With US support, Taiwan successfully defended Kinmen, and the crisis gradually eased.

events.title: Economic Miracle Period
events.description: Taiwan developed from agricultural to industrial society, export-oriented economy grew rapidly. Taiwan became one of the 'Four Asian Tigers,' achieving dramatic economic growth.

events.title: Kaohsiung Export Processing Zone Established
events.description: Taiwan's first export processing zone was established in Kaohsiung, attracting foreign investment and developing export industries. This promoted Taiwan's industrialization and economic takeoff.

events.title: ROC Withdraws from UN
events.description: The UN General Assembly passed Resolution 2758, the PRC replaced the ROC as China's representative in the UN. The ROC withdrew from the UN, entering diplomatic isolation.

events.title: Death of Chiang Kai-shek
events.description: ROC President Chiang Kai-shek died aged 87. Vice President Yen Chia-kan succeeded as president, Chiang Ching-kuo controlled actual power and continued authoritarian rule.

events.title: Kaohsiung Incident
events.description: Opposition magazine Formosa held a Human Rights Day rally in Kaohsiung, leading to violent clashes. Government arrested many opposition leaders, but the incident became a turning point for Taiwan's democratization.

events.title: US Switches Recognition to PRC
events.description: The US established diplomatic relations with the PRC and severed relations with the ROC. But the US passed the Taiwan Relations Act, continuing unofficial relations and security commitments.

events.title: Democratic Progressive Party Founded
events.description: Despite martial law banning new parties, opposition figures established the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), becoming Taiwan's first opposition party. This was a milestone in Taiwan's democratization.

events.title: Martial Law Lifted
events.description: Chiang Ching-kuo announced the lifting of martial law, ending 38 years of military rule. Taiwan entered a new era of democratization, with freedoms of speech and assembly guaranteed.

events.title: Mainland Visit Ban Lifted
events.description: The government lifted the ban on visiting mainland China, allowing separated families to reunite. This opened cross-strait people-to-people exchanges.

events.title: Lee Teng-hui Becomes President
events.description: After Chiang Ching-kuo's death, Vice President Lee Teng-hui succeeded as president, becoming Taiwan's first Taiwanese-born president. Lee promoted democratic reform and localization.

events.title: End of Period of National Mobilization
events.description: The government announced the end of the 'Period of National Mobilization for Suppression of the Communist Rebellion,' terminating the temporary provisions. This was an important step in Taiwan's constitutional normalization.

events.title: Full Legislative Yuan Re-election
events.description: Taiwan held its first full Legislative Yuan election, ending the 'senior legislators' era. This completed parliamentary democratization.

events.title: Third Taiwan Strait Crisis
events.description: The PRC conducted missile tests and military exercises in the Taiwan Strait to oppose Lee Teng-hui's visit to the US and Taiwan's first presidential election. The US dispatched aircraft carrier groups to respond, easing the crisis.

events.title: First Direct Presidential Election
events.description: Taiwan held its first direct presidential election, with Lee Teng-hui winning. This was the first free democratic presidential election in Chinese society, of great significance.

events.title: 921 Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck central Taiwan, killing over 2,400 people and destroying numerous buildings. This was Taiwan's most serious earthquake disaster in the 20th century.

events.title: First Power Transition
events.description: DPP candidate Chen Shui-bian was elected president, ending the KMT's over 50-year rule in Taiwan. This was Taiwan's first power transition, proving democratic consolidation.

events.title: Ma Ying-jeou Elected President
events.description: KMT candidate Ma Ying-jeou was elected president, marking the second power transition. Ma promoted closer cross-strait relations, signing multiple economic agreements with mainland China.

events.title: Sunflower Student Movement
events.description: Students occupied the Legislative Yuan to oppose the Cross-Strait Service Trade Agreement, lasting 24 days. This movement demonstrated civil society's strength and influenced Taiwan's politics.

events.title: Tsai Ing-wen Elected President
events.description: DPP's Tsai Ing-wen was elected president, becoming Taiwan's first female president. The DPP simultaneously gained a majority in the Legislative Yuan, governing completely for the first time.

events.title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalized
events.description: Taiwan became Asia's first jurisdiction to legalize same-sex marriage. The Act for Implementation of Judicial Yuan Interpretation No. 748 was passed, protecting same-sex couples' marriage rights.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Prevention Success
events.description: Taiwan successfully controlled COVID-19 spread, maintaining normal life while other countries suffered severe outbreaks. Taiwan's pandemic prevention experience gained international acclaim.

events.title: Tsai Ing-wen Re-elected
events.description: President Tsai Ing-wen was re-elected with a historic high vote count. The DPP maintained its majority in the Legislative Yuan, continuing to govern.
